text:
paul: Quickstart broke in our student sandbox VMs. redwoodctl login errors when saving profile to project-mounted HOME.

paul: Output: 
```
error: unable to persist profile: open /workspace/.config/redwood/profiles.json: permission denied
failed to replace file atomically: permission denied
```

leila: Oof. Is the repo mounted as a different owner? We hit this with workshop VMs where user accounts are ephemeral and the repo is owned by another uid.

paul: Yep, /workspace is owned by uid 1000 but the runner uses uid 1002. Previously redwoodctl fell back to non-atomic writes; now it hard-fails.

rahim: Also noticed when teaching, the device-code auth TTL (60s) is too short — students take longer to open the link and paste the code. When it expires the CLI exits with no clear retry command. Example: 
```
Visit https://auth.redwood.ai/device and enter code: HJKL-98YT
Waiting for authorization...
error: device code expired
```

nico: Thanks for reporting. Two immediate DX improvements: (1) detect EXDEV/EACCES and automatically fallback to safe, non-atomic write mode with a WARN message and sample remediation; (2) make device flow friendlier in interactive sessions and add a headless/CI mode that accepts a pre-generated token or extends TTL.

leila: For workshops the friendly text should be a single line so instructors can grep CI logs. Suggestion: "config not writable; try `export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/redwood && redwoodctl login` or use `--in-memory` for ephemeral environments". Also return an exit code that signals a recoverable auth problem.

paul: Workaround we used: `mkdir -p /tmp/rwd && XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/rwd redwoodctl login --profile workshop`. That works but is not discoverable for students.

rahim: Could CLI auto-detect common CI/env vars (CI=1, GITHUB_ACTIONS) or detect mounted home to prefer non-atomic writes? I think auto-fallback would drastically reduce onboarding friction.

nico: From the engineering side: implement a cheap probe at startup that attempts to create+rename a temp file in config dir. If probe fails with EACCES/EXDEV, switch to safe-write path and log a concise remediation hint. Add flags: `--profile-path`, `--no-atomic`, `--in-memory` and `--device-ttl-seconds` for workshops. Also add `--headless-token PATH` to read a token file in CI.

paul: I'll attach a tiny Dockerfile + demo script to the GH issue. Dockerfile snippet: 
```
FROM debian:12
RUN useradd -m -u 1002 student
USER student
WORKDIR /workspace
COPY . /workspace
ENV HOME=/home/student
CMD ["/bin/sh", "-c", "redwoodctl login --profile workshop"]
```

bot-auth: (automated) job #77 failed: onboard-sandbox  auth: write permission to config. Logs: https://ci.internal/job/77

leila: For docs/quickstart we should add a small troubleshooting section: "If login fails with permission denied when saving profile, run: `export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/redwood && redwoodctl login` or use `--in-memory` and follow with `redwoodctl persist --path /tmp/token.json`."

rahim: I'll open the GH issue with repro and include a unit test idea: stub os.Rename to return EXDEV/EACCES and assert that we log the one-line XDG suggestion and use safe-write. @nico can you own the test + issue?

nico: Yep, I'll file the issue and add the unit test. Long term we should also make device flow print a clickable link when TERM supports it and increase TTL in interactive terminals.

paul: Thanks everyone — short-term fix is to set XDG_CONFIG_HOME in the workshop bootstrap. Medium-term: auto-fallback + headless flags.
